title: Airbus A320 - 214 · Philadelphia, PA (2014)
summary: Before pushback from the gate, the first officer, who was the pilot monitoring, initialized the flight management computer (FMC) and mistakenly entered the incorrect departure runway (27R instead of the assigned 27L). As the captain taxied onto runway 27L for departure, he noticed that the wrong runway was entered in the FMC. The captain asked the first officer to correct the runway entry in the FMC, which she completed about 27 seconds before the beginning of the takeoff roll; however, she did not enter the FLEX temperature (a reduced takeoff thrust setting) for the newly entered runway or upload the related V-speeds.
probable_cause: the captain's decision to reject the takeoff after the airplane had rotated. Contributing to the accident was the flight crew's failure to follow standard operating procedures by not verifying that the airplane's flight management computer was properly configured for takeoff and the captain's failure to perform the correct action in response to the electronic centralized aircraft monitoring alert.

summary: The pilots of the twin-engine airplane were conducting a cross-country instrument flight rules (IFR) flight. Although both pilots were instrument-rated and IFR-current, the right seat pilot had only 8.8 hours of actual instrument experience, and the left seat pilot had only 1.8 hours of actual instrument experience. Also causal was the pilots' failure to maintain control of the airplane while operating in instrument flight rules (IFR) conditions, likely due to spatial disorientation, following the failure of the vacuum pump. title: 2014 Armenian Mil Mi-24 shootdown
summary: An Armenian Mil Mi-24 attack helicopter was shot down by Azerbaijani Armed Forces with an Igla-S MANPAD surface-to-air missile during the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict. According to Armenian officials, the helicopter was not armed and was participating in military exercises without having entered hostile territory. British analyst Thomas de Waal described the shootdown as the worst military incident in more than 20 years, stating the helicopter was shot down in no-man's land after breaking an informal five-kilometer no-fly zone.
probable_cause: Hostile fire from Azerbaijani forces using a portable air defense system.

events.text: Armenian Mil Mi-24 helicopter was participating in the week-long joint Armenian-NKR Unity 2014 military exercises in the disputed region.

According to British analyst Thomas de Waal, the helicopter was shot down in the no-man's land between the two armies after breaking into an informal five-kilometer no-fly zone the two sides had agreed on.
Two Mi-24s were flying parallel to the line of contact as the launch of a surface-to-air missile, identified as an Igla-S MANPAD, was heard off screen.
